name: STAR Assurance — two-body propagator audit
summary: Differential audit of Kepler propagators (hapsira farnocchia and vallado, Orekit KeplerianPropagator, NAIF prop2b, S.T.A.R.) against the closed-form state of 450 known orbits, including 10 whole revolutions, with probe validation on a published example and a deadline that records solvers which never answer.
reference: Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, Example 2-4: r = (-4219.7527, 4363.0292, -3958.7666) km, v = (3.689866, -1.916735, -6.112511) km/s after 40 min; truth = closed-form state of a known orbit
reference_observed: all 5 implementations reproduce the printed state within 4.8e-5 km; a synthetic propagator with a 1e-9 clock-rate error passes the probe and is exposed only after 10 revolutions

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: km, km/s, s, radians internally; km^3/s^2
review.G-06: corpus generated in-repo from closed-form equations, fingerprint of the rounded corpus pinned
review.G-08: subprocess only for the audited solver; inputs via stdin; runner names prefixed
review.G-13: failed run raises with stderr tail; non-finite or wrong-length answer is a refusal; hostile inputs run alone with a deadline (error:Hang); a propagator failing the probe is not compared
